title: Epidemiology and Subtype Distribution of Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Children Aged 0-36 Months With Severe Acute Respiratory Infection in Mato Grosso do Sul, a Brazilian Border State, 2022-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUND: RSV is a leading cause of severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) in children. We describe RSV-associated SARI in children up to 36 months, including seasonality, A/B subtyping, and clinical profile, in Mato Grosso do Sul, a Brazilian border state. METHODS: This retrospective, surveillance-based descriptive study used SIVEP-Gripe data on RSV-positive SARI cases notified in 2022-2024. A convenience subset of preserved samples with Ct ≤ 27 (313 typed; 13.9% of cases) underwent duplex RT-qPCR typing. Seasonality was assessed with quasi-Poisson regression; clinical features were compared using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests and Wilcoxon tests. RESULTS: Among 9758 SARI cases, 2254 (23%) were RSV positive. Peak activity was highest in 2023 (Week 14). Most cases (75%) occurred in infants younger than 12 months. Among cases with information, 79.5% (1502/1889) received ventilatory support (8.4% invasive), 14.2% (294/2076) required ICU admission, and 37 died (case fatality 1.6%). From July 2023, with all samples tested for rhinovirus, adenovirus, and human metapneumovirus, 18.4% of cases had codetection, mostly rhinovirus. Among typed samples, RSV-B accounted for 31/37 in 2022 and 104/137 in 2024, and RSV-A accounted for 131/138 in 2023. Deaths among typed cases (6/170 RSV-A and 0/142 RSV-B) all occurred in 2023. CONCLUSIONS: RSV was a frequent cause of SARI hospitalization in this Brazilian border state, mainly among infants. RSV-A and RSV-B cocirculated with comparable clinical profiles; subtype-specific mortality could not be assessed because all deaths among typed cases occurred in 2023. Typed samples were a non-random subset, and clinical data had missing values.

title: RSV prevention after nirsevimab: what Europe has learned-and what it has not.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Europe moved within two seasons from selective respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prophylaxis for a small high-risk group to population-based strategies capable of protecting most infants. We aimed to examine the European experience with RSV prevention after nirsevimab introduction, and identify key lessons regarding implementation, programme performance, comparative evaluation, and remaining evidence gaps. Studies evaluating RSV prevention after nirsevimab introduction in Europe were searched. Evidence was mapped according to implementation strategies, effectiveness outcomes, healthcare impact, safety, resistance, and emerging research questions. Real-world studies from Europe consistently reported considerable reductions in RSV hospitalisation and intensive-care admission following nirsevimab implementation. Heterogeneity in programme design and delivery suggests that product effectiveness is only one determinant of impact: programme characteristics like administration timing, catch-up strategies, coverage, maternity-versus-community delivery, and the age distribution of baseline burden influence observed outcomes. Second-season evidence distinguishes limited residual individual protection from a persisting cumulative two-season benefit. Maternal RSVpreF vaccination is highly effective when administered sufficiently before delivery, although cross-strategy comparisons remain vulnerable to timing and selection bias. Safety findings remain reassuring; resistance-associated substitutions are detectable but have not undermined population-level effectiveness. The recent introduction of clesrovimab further expands preventive options. CONCLUSION: Europe has answered whether universal infant RSV prevention can reduce severe disease burden but not yet standardised how programmes are compared. The next phase should move from product advocacy to programme science: one primary strategy for most infants, explicit rescue indications, linked immunisation-outcome-genomic surveillance, common estimands and transparent measurement of equity and opportunity cost. WHAT IS KNOWN: • Long-acting monoclonal antibodies and maternal RSVpreF vaccination prevent severe RSV disease in early infancy. WHAT IS NEW: • The European lesson is not a universal product ranking: delivery architecture, catch-up and the interval between maternal vaccination and birth determine population impact. • Second-season policy requires estimand discipline: limited residual effectiveness can coexist with substantial cumulative two-season benefit and no rebound.

title: Harnessing mucosal and systemic immunity against respiratory viruses: vaccine platforms, delivery strategies, and adjuvants.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Long-lasting immunity against respiratory viruses, including influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus, remains a challenge. Effective vaccines and vaccination strategies that confer durable protection against these viruses require the induction of both systemic and mucosal immunity. AREA COVERED: This review covers the latest trends in respiratory viral vaccine platforms, including modified virus-like particles and mRNA-based vaccines, as well as adjuvants, and new vaccination strategies that induce systemic and mucosal immunity and generate lung-resident memory cells. A better understanding of innate immune responses to vaccination is critical for improving vaccine efficacy and safety and for identifying early predictive correlates. EXPERT OPINION: This article outlines recent advances and approaches to developing next-generation respiratory viral vaccines and new vaccination strategies to induce systemic and mucosal immunity. It also discusses the gap between preclinical and clinical outcomes of mucosal vaccination.

title: Pathogens associated with childhood febrile illness in West Africa: a systematic review
abstract: Background Up to 80% of children seeking medical attention in Africa present with acute febrile illness. Epidemiological data on the locally circulating pathogens causing fever are essential to inform clinical management and for public health interventions. This systematic review sought to understand the aetiologies of febrile illness among children in West Africa. Methods We included healthcare facility and community-based studies with cross-sectional, case-control, and retrospective cross-sectional design which used laboratory methods to detect pathogens causing fever in children aged 1 month to 15 years. A literature search was conducted in Medline and Embase via OVID, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Connecting Repositories (CoRE), Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), African Journals Online (AJOL) and World Health Organisation (WHO) Africa Index Medicus, for studies published from 2013 to 2023. Data was extracted on pathogens detected from routine clinical investigations and study-specific laboratory testing. A risk of bias assessment was conducted using a consolidated CASP checklist developed from the case-control and cross-sectional study checklists. Results We included 84 studies from 11 West African countries. 42% of studies investigated bacterial pathogens in blood, 24% in respiratory samples and 19% in urine, stool, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and ear swabs combined, resulting in the detection of 25 different bacterial species. The most common of these were Salmonella enterica, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, Haemophilus influenzae, and Escherichia coli. Seventeen different viruses were detected. Dengue virus, chikungunya virus and West Nile virus were mostly detected from serological studies. Influenza viruses, rhinoviruses, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza viruses, human metapneumovirus, coronaviruses, adenoviruses, and enteroviruses were commonly isolated from respiratory samples. Plasmodium falciparum was the most abundant parasite of the 5 different parasites/fungal species detected. Only 8% of studies performed comprehensive investigations (concurrent testing across ≥ 3 pathogen classes in the same participant) for a wide range of pathogens. Conclusion This study found that diagnostic testing was predominantly blood-based, with limited investigation of gastrointestinal, zoonotic, and emerging pathogens. These findings reveal important gaps in the existing evidence base for febrile pathogen detection and highlight areas where future primary research with a broader diagnostic scope would provide more complete epidemiological data. This systematic review has been registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) under the registration number: CRD 42023466517. abstract_zh: 背景 在非洲就医的儿童中,高达 80% 患有急性发热性疾病。有关当地传播的发烧病原体的流行病学数据对于临床管理和公共卫生干预至关重要。这项系统评价旨在了解西非儿童发热性疾病的病因。方法 我们纳入了医疗机构和社区研究,采用横断面、病例对照和回顾性横断面设计,使用实验室方法检测引起 1 个月至 15 岁儿童发烧的病原体。通过 OVID、Scopus、ScienceDirect、Connecting Repositories (CoRE)、Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ)、African Journals Online (AJOL) 和世界卫生组织 (WHO) Africa Index Medicus 在 Medline 和 Embase 上进行了文献检索,检索 2013 年至 2023 年发表的研究。数据是从常规临床调查和特定研究实验室测试中检测到的病原体中提取的。使用根据病例对照和横断面研究清单开发的综合 CASP 清单进行偏倚风险评估。结果 我们纳入了来自 11 个西非国家的 84 项研究。42% 的研究调查了血液中的细菌病原体,24% 的研究调查了呼吸道样本中的细菌病原体,19% 的研究调查了尿液、粪便、脑脊液 (CSF) 和耳拭子中的细菌病原体,最终检测到了 25 种不同的细菌。其中最常见的是肠道沙门氏菌、肺炎链球菌、金黄色葡萄球菌、流感嗜血杆菌和大肠杆菌。检测到十七种不同的病毒。登革热病毒、基孔肯雅病毒和西尼罗河病毒主要是通过血清学研究检测到的。通常从呼吸道样本中分离出流感病毒、鼻病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、副流感病毒、人偏肺病毒、冠状病毒、腺病毒和肠道病毒。恶性疟原虫是检测到的 5 种不同寄生虫/真菌物种中最丰富的寄生虫。只有 8% 的研究对多种病原体进行了全面调查(同一参与者同时测试 ≥ 3 种病原体类别)。结论 这项研究发现诊断检测主要以血液为基础,对胃肠道、人畜共患和新出现的病原体的研究有限。这些发现揭示了发热病原体检测的现有证据基础中的重要差距,并强调了未来具有更广泛诊断范围的初级研究将提供更完整的流行病学数据的领域。该系统评价已在国际前瞻性系统评价注册库(PROSPERO)中注册,注册号:CRD 42023466517。临床试验注册 不适用

title: A divergent bat orthopneumovirus with zoonotic potential constrained by RSV adaptive immunity and broad-spectrum treatment.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; genus Orthopneumovirus) causes severe pneumonia in young children worldwide, yet the zoonotic potential of the few known nonhuman animal orthopneumoviruses remains unknown. Here, we characterized a highly divergent bat orthopneumovirus (BPV) from West African straw-colored fruit bats and established a systematic framework for evaluating zoonotic risk posed by an emerging viral pathogen. Epidemiologic data in bats showed a low viral detection rate (24 of 1778 RT-PCR positive) and low seroprevalence (6 of 66 IgG IFA positive), suggesting BPV episodic circulation potentially sustained in immunologically naïve bats following bat birthing events. Near-complete genomes from two BPV genetic variants revealed prototypic orthopneumovirus organization, but lacked the SH viroporin-encoding gene present in RSV. Functional experiments showed that BPV NS1/NS2 antagonized human interferon β responses, and that BPV pseudoviruses entered human cells (4.5- to 53.5-fold less efficiently than RSV), while being cross-neutralized by human RSV-reactive antisera, together suggesting zoonotic traits that may be partly constrained by cross-protective immunity. BPV escaped neutralization by RSV-specific therapeutic palivizumab and inhibition by lonafarnib, but remained susceptible to MPE8, a broad-spectrum monoclonal antibody that targets the conserved pneumovirus antigenic site III. These findings identify zoonotic traits of a divergent bat pneumovirus while suggesting potential protective value of preexisting RSV immunity and broad-spectrum interventions, which has implications for pandemic preparedness. Whether cross-protection in the human population may change by the advent of RSV vaccination warrants investigation. Efforts to investigate orthopneumovirus host shifts, reservoir studies, and development of broadly reactive orthopneumovirus vaccines and antivirals are warranted.

title: Generative AI-Driven Hybrid Optimized Deep Learning Model for Computational Intelligence Predicting HMPV Virus Infections in Healthcare
abstract: Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a major etiology of acute respiratory illness, especially among high-risk groups like young children, the elderly, and immunocompromised patients. Despite its prevalence, HMPV diagnosis is not always accurate due to nonspecific clinical presentation and lack of routine testing, with many cases going undetected or being detected late. Accurate and timely prediction of HMPV infection is important for improving patient outcomes and optimizing healthcare interventions. This paper introduces an innovative AI-based hybrid deep learning framework that integrates Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), CNN-RNN architectures, and Quantum-Inspired Support Vector Machines (QSVM) for precise HMPV prediction. Our approach resolves fundamental problems in medical AI, such as data insufficiency, class imbalance, interpretability, and real-time processing, by introducing three innovations: (1) GAN-based synthetic data augmentation for realistic patient record generation without destroying clinical relationships, substantially boosting the diversity and robustness of training data; (2) a hybrid CNN-RNN model for spatiotemporal feature extraction from multimodal clinical data sources such as Electronic Health Records (EHRs), time-series vitals, and chest X-rays to enable end-to-end pattern recognition and sequence analysis; and (3) QSVM optimization for improved classification in high-dimensional spaces by exploiting quantum-inspired decision boundaries to realize superior separability and minimize misclassification rates. The suggested model has 96.2% accuracy, 96.1% F1-score, and 0.983 AUC-ROC, 5%–7% higher than traditional approaches and 32% fewer false negatives, hence minimizing the chance of undetected instances. To ensure model robustness and generalizability, rigorous cross-validation was conducted across various hospital networks and patient populations. Clinical three-hospital network validation attests to the strength and scalability of the model, with real-time inference times (<200ms) enabling smooth integration into EHR systems and rapid clinical decision support. Further, attention mechanisms integrated into the CNN-RNN model enhance interpretability by highlighting essential features that influence predictions, 59 thereby closing the loop between AI-derived insights and medical reasoning and increasing clinician confidence. The integration of generative augmentation, hybrid modeling, and quantum-inspired optimization makes our framework a state-of-the-art solution for predictive healthcare, significantly improving the early detection and treatment of HMPV infections.

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation: Outcomes in a 15‐Year Single‐Center Cohort
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a frequent and potentially severe complication after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT). We describe outcomes in a 15-year single-center cohort. METHODS: All allo-HCT recipients with PCR-confirmed RSV infection at Karolinska University Hospital (January 2010-April 2024) were analyzed retrospectively. Outcomes were evaluated by time from HCT; ribavirin analyses were restricted to patients with upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) at presentation, at risk of progression to lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI). RESULTS: Among 102 patients, 44 (43%) were diagnosed more than 1 year after HCT. Overall, 28 (27%) developed LRTI, including eight who progressed from URTI. RSV-associated mortality was 2/102 (2.0%); ICU admission occurred in 6/102 (5.9%). Progression from URTI to LRTI was more frequent when RSV was diagnosed within 30 days of HCT than later (4/11 [36%] vs. 4/71 [5.6%]; p = 0.010). Of 43 patients given ribavirin (predominantly oral), 31 were treated at the URTI stage; 5/31 (16%) progressed after initiation versus 2/51 (3.9%) untreated (p = 0.098). CRP was higher in LRTI than in URTI alone (median 50 vs. 17 mg/L; p = 0.011), but bacterial co-infection was also more frequent (32% vs. CONCLUSION: RSV-associated mortality after allo-HCT was low, but morbidity was prolonged, particularly early after transplantation. Findings should be interpreted cautiously given the late occurrence of RSV in many patients and differences in diagnostics and transplant practice compared with historical cohorts. This retrospective study did not show a protective effect of oral ribavirin. Prospective studies of prevention and treatment, including RSV vaccination, are warranted.

title: Aligned Evidence, Aligned Guidance: 2026-2027 Respiratory Virus Immunization Recommendations from The AAFP, AAP, ACOG, AND IDSA.
abstract: Disruption of the federal vaccine advisory process prompted a coordinated, society-led approach to respiratory virus immunization guidance for the 2026-2027 season. The Vaccine Integrity Project (VIP) at the University of Minnesota Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy, in collaboration with the American Medical Association and with coordination support from the Council of Medical Specialty Societies, completed systematic reviews of influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization. Across 299 studies, the reviews confirmed protection against hospitalization and death and identified no new safety concerns in comparative studies. On September 2, 2026, the American Academy of Family Physicians (AAFP), American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Infectious Diseases Society of America issued aligned recommendations informed by this evidence. This report explains the shared evidence base, summarizes recommendations by age and population, describes the AAFP review and adoption process, and directs primary care clinicians to implementation and patient resources.

title: Diverse lung challenges elicit a conserved monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation blueprint.
abstract: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) form a first line of defense to lung insults. These insults often lead to replacement of fetal-derived tissue-resident AMs (fAMs) by monocyte-derived AMs (mono-AMs) with different functionality, which impacts lung immunity during future lung challenges. However, whether these alterations are conserved or insult specific is not well understood. Here we show that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection remodels the AM compartment long term. We perform comparative analyses of fAMs and mono-AMs after RSV infection, influenza A virus infection or clodronate liposome administration and identify a crucial tissue integration checkpoint of CD11b+ mono-AMs that involves acquisition of proliferative capacity and requires EGR2-mediated transcriptional rewiring. Mono-AMs elicited by RSV, influenza A virus or clodronate liposomes have a hardwired ontogeny-dependent stereotypical profile of transcription, proliferation, metabolism and enhanced immunoreactivity despite a substantially different inflammatory environment during differentiation; accordingly, mono-AMs elicited by sterile or infectious insult protect from subsequent Streptococcus pneumoniae infection. By contrast, fAMs display context-dependent transcriptional alterations. Our findings highlight that long-term changes in the AM compartment show origin-dependent phenotypic divergence and that mono-AM integration follows a hardwired trajectory fine-tuned by environmental factors.

title: Risk of respiratory infections in closed communities: multi-dimensional risk assessment and integrated surveillance in a nursing home and a prison (Stell-ARI project)
abstract: Viral Acute Respiratory Infections (ARIs) are particularly relevant for people living in closed and vulnerable communities. The Stell-ARI Project aimed to design and apply a multi-dimensional framework integrating environmental risk assessment (based on building structure and management, resident population characteristics, indoor air quality (IAQ), and microbiological contamination of air and surfaces) with wastewater-based and clinical surveillance for SARS-CoV-2, Human Adenovirus (HAdV), Influenza Virus A (IVA) and B (IVB), Respiratory Syncytial Virus A (RSVA) and B (RSVB). This system was applied in two pilot institutional communities: a nursing home and a prison. The study design included questionnaire surveys of facility managers, residents and workers alongside environmental monitoring of chemical and microbial contaminants. Domain-specific and global risk scores were calculated. Scores were lower in the nursing home than in the prison for building structure and management (3 vs. 13) and resident population characteristics (3.4 vs. The chemical air risk score showed similar differences (1.3 vs. 3.0) and the two settings also differed in their indoor pollutant profiles. The microbiological air and surface risk score was also better in nursing home (4.0 vs 5.0). In both settings, a COVID-19 cluster was detected and SARS-CoV-2 and HAdV were found in air and surface samples, as well as in wastewater, not only in coincidence with clinical cases, but throughout the monitoring period, with a higher frequency in nursing home. In conclusion, this novel multi-dimensional structured approach, although needing further validation, represents a potential operational tool to support ARIs surveillance, prevention and control in closed and vulnerable institutional communities.

title: Post-pandemic shifts in respiratory pathogens and peripheral immune correlates among hospitalized children with ALRTI: a retrospective molecular surveillance study in northern China, 2023–2024
abstract: Background Post-pandemic respiratory pathogen circulation has changed, but concurrent molecular and immune data remain limited. We examined pathogen trends and peripheral immune correlates in children hospitalized with acute lower respiratory tract infection (ALRTI) in northern China during 2023–2024. Methods This single-centre retrospective study included 604 hospitalization episodes. A 13-target multiplex nucleic-acid panel defined pathogen groups. Immunoglobulins, lymphocyte subsets and inflammatory markers were compared across monoinfection, mixed infection (≥2 pathogen categories) and panel-negative groups. Immune comparisons adjusted for age, sex and year using regression with cluster-robust standard errors for repeated admissions and false-discovery-rate correction. Annual trends were assessed using age-standardised rates and logistic regression adjusted for age, sex and calendar month. Results Among 601 complete-panel episodes, 528 (87.9%) had a detected pathogen. Mycoplasma pneumoniae predominated (43.4%), followed by rhinovirus (23.6%) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; 14.3%). pneumoniae detection increased from 32.4% in 2023 to 54.3% in 2024, while RSV decreased from 21.4% to 7.3% (both q < 0.001). Annual shifts persisted after age standardisation and covariate adjustment: adjusted odds ratios for 2024 vs. 2023 were 3.09 (95% CI, 1.94–4.94) for M. pneumoniae, 0.29 (0.16–0.53) for RSV and 0.13 (0.03–0.53) for influenza A. Mixed infection (21.5%) decreased with age (adjusted odds ratio per year, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.86–0.98). After adjustment and multiplicity correction, M. pneumoniae and mixed infections were associated with higher immunoglobulin M. Rhinovirus monoinfection was associated with lower total T-cell and CD8+ T-cell percentages and higher B-cell percentage; mixed infection was associated with lower total T-cell percentage. Cytokine analyses were exploratory because approximately 35% of episodes were tested. Conclusion Pathogen profiles shifted substantially between 2023 and 2024, supporting continued molecular surveillance and age-aware interpretation of immune measures. Because the panel did not cover typical bacterial pathogens, panel-negative episodes should not be equated with absence of infection.
